Class IndexFormat

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.IndexFormat
public final class IndexFormat extends Object
The on-disk layout of MICRONAUT-INF/index.bin, the index a runner jar carries so that the launcher never has to parse a nested archive's central directory at startup.

This class is the single contract shared by the writer (in the packaging library) and the reader (in the launcher). It contains constants only: every member is a compile-time constant, so javac inlines them at every use site and this class is never loaded at runtime.

Conventions

  • All multi-byte integers are little-endian.
  • u8/u16/u32/u64 denote unsigned values; readers widen them (u32 into a long where the value may exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE).
  • Every section begins at an 8-byte aligned offset relative to the start of the index.
  • A string reference (strref) is a u32 byte offset into the string table. A string is stored as u16 length followed by that many UTF-8 bytes. Offset 0 always holds the empty string, so a strref of 0 means "absent".
  • A string list reference is a u32 offset into the string table of a u16 count followed by count u32 string references.
  • NO_INDEX is the sentinel for an absent record index.

Logical names

An entry's logical name is its name relative to the jar that contains it. For nested jars that is the entry name as stored in the nested archive; for jar 0 (the application layer, stored exploded in the outer archive) it is the outer entry name minus the MICRONAUT-INF/classes/ prefix. Lookups are always by logical name.

Multi-release jars

For a jar flagged JAR_FLAG_MULTI_RELEASE, every META-INF/versions/N/<path> entry whose <path> does not itself start with META-INF/ is indexed a second time under the logical name <path> as an alias record carrying ENTRY_FLAG_VERSIONED_ALIAS and mrVersion = N. Within one jar, alias records precede the base record in descending version order, so a lookup walks the chain and takes the first record whose mrVersion is 0 or at most the effective runtime feature version.

Since:
1.0

  • Method Details

    • hash

      public static int hash(String name)
      The hash of a logical name, as stored in E_NAME_HASH and used to pick a hash table slot.

      It is String.hashCode(), whose value is specified by the Java language, spread so that the high bits influence the low-order slot index. Writers and readers must agree exactly, so the definition is fixed here and must never change within a format version.

      Parameters:
      name - the logical name
      Returns:
      the hash

    • spread

      public static int spread(int hashCode)
      Mixes the high bits of a String.hashCode() into the low bits.
      Parameters:
      hashCode - the raw hash code
      Returns:
      the spread hash
